title: Quadrilaterals
prerequisites: Angle sum property of a triangle.
Properties of parallel lines and a transversal.
Familiarity with the terms diagonal and vertex.

topics.title: Types of Quadrilaterals and the Parallelogram
topics.quick_summary: The angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360°, and a parallelogram has opposite sides and angles equal with diagonals that bisect each other.
topics.real_life: A collapsible scissor gate stays a parallelogram at every stage of opening — opposite sides remain equal even as the angles change.

detailed.definition: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral in which both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. A rhombus is a parallelogram with all sides equal, a rectangle one with all angles right angles, and a square is both.
detailed.key_idea: The family is hierarchical: every square is a rhombus and a rectangle, and every rhombus and rectangle is a parallelogram. Properties inherit downward but not upward.
detailed.working_principle: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if any one of these holds: both pairs of opposite sides equal, both pairs of opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect each other, or one pair of opposite sides both equal and parallel.
applications: Diagonals of a rectangle are equal; of a rhombus, perpendicular; of a square, both.
A diagonal divides a parallelogram into two congruent triangles.
The angle sum of any quadrilateral is 360°.

points: Parallelogram: opposite sides equal, opposite angles equal, diagonals bisect each other.
Rectangle: diagonals are equal. Rhombus: diagonals are perpendicular bisectors.
Square: diagonals are equal AND perpendicular bisectors.
One pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is enough to prove a parallelogram.
mistakes: Saying the diagonals of a parallelogram are equal; only in a rectangle are they equal.
Assuming the diagonals of a rhombus are equal; they are perpendicular, not equal.
Calling a trapezium a parallelogram; only one pair of its sides is parallel.
topics.memory_hook: 'Square = Rectangle + Rhombus' — it inherits equal diagonals from one and perpendicular diagonals from the other.
topics.advanced: In vector terms, a quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram exactly when AB⃗ = DC⃗. Every classical property then follows in one or two lines of vector algebra.

topics.title: The Mid-point Theorem
topics.quick_summary: The line joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half its length.
topics.real_life: A shelf fixed halfway up two sloping supports is automatically parallel to the floor and half the span — the mid-point theorem doing carpentry.

detailed.definition: Mid-point theorem: the segment joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and equal to half of it. Its converse states that a line through the mid-point of one side, parallel to another side, bisects the third side.
detailed.key_idea: The theorem converts a statement about lengths into one about parallels, and its converse does the reverse. Most quadrilateral proofs use one or the other to create a parallelogram.
detailed.working_principle: In a quadrilateral, joining the mid-points of all four sides always produces a parallelogram, whatever the original shape. This is proved by applying the mid-point theorem to the two triangles formed by a diagonal.
applications: The figure formed by joining the mid-points of any quadrilateral is a parallelogram.
Mid-points of a rectangle give a rhombus; of a rhombus, a rectangle.
The converse is used to prove that a point is a mid-point.

points: Mid-point theorem: segment joining mid-points is parallel to and half the third side.
Converse: a line through one mid-point parallel to another side bisects the third side.
Joining mid-points of any quadrilateral gives a parallelogram.
Mid-points of a rectangle form a rhombus; mid-points of a rhombus form a rectangle.
The theorem is proved using congruent triangles or by constructing a parallelogram.
mistakes: Forgetting the 'half the length' part and stating only parallelism.
Applying the converse without confirming the parallel condition.
Assuming the mid-point figure of a square is a square of half the area; it is a square of half the area, but the same is not true for other shapes.
topics.memory_hook: 'Join the mid-points: parallel to the third side, and exactly half of it.'
topics.advanced: The mid-point theorem is the simplest case of the basic proportionality theorem, which allows any ratio rather than just one-half. Class 10 similarity generalises this chapter almost entirely.
